question_text: Pure Al has ρAl=2.71 g/cm³ and pure Li has ρLi=0.534 g/cm³.  An Al–Li alloy is desired to have an overall density of 2.47 g/cm³.  What weight percent Li must be added?The unit of the answer is wt%.
response:
Using ideal volume mixing (the standard rule of mixtures for density):

$$\frac{1}{\rho} = \frac{w_{\text{Al}}}{\rho_{\text{Al}}} + \frac{w_{\text{Li}}}{\rho_{\text{Li}}}, \quad w_{\text{Al}} = 1 - w_{\text{Li}}}$$

Solving for the Li weight fraction:

$$w_{\text{Li}} = \frac{\tfrac{1}{\rho} - \tfrac{1}{\rho_{\text{Al}}}}{\tfrac{1}{\rho_{\text{Li}}} - \tfrac{1}{\rho_{\text{Al}}}} = \frac{\tfrac{1}{2.47} - \tfrac{1}{2.71}}{\tfrac{1}{0.534} - \tfrac{1}{2.71}} \approx 0.0238$$

$$\boxed{2.38}$$
